title: PG-09.1 Identity, admission and ACFA boundary (memev)
request: Programme contract for work package WP09 in memev: Identity, admission and ACFA boundary. Proposed and unsigned; the signer signs it after the red-team gate. Source: the programme decomposition of 31 Oct 2026 (docs/scope-one/programme/WBS.md, docs/scope-one/programme/DECOMPOSITION.md, docs/scope-one/programme/fragments/WP09.json) and the owner notes behind docs/scope-one/programme/REQUIREMENTS.md. Depends on tasks outside this contract: WP04-02, WP06-02. Covers only what the Scope One contracts (SO-1.01 to SO-1.11) do not already cover; the mapping is in contracts/programme/manifest.json. Boundary with SO-2.12: WP09-02 (the contribution-admission boundary) is a prerequisite of federated computation and is not repeated there. Signed vault contract MEM-145, MEM-146 and MEM-147 (cited by id only): foundation: human binding of agent roles; WP09-01 reuses it. Signed vault contract WO-05-D (cited by id only): the external trust service specification; the adapters of WP09-02 and WP09-03 sit on its boundary and this spec does not specify the service. Build layer (owner delegation, 1 Nov 2026): the unsigned fold (SO-A-01 to SO-A-12, SO-R-E, SO-F-01 to SO-F-13, cited by id only) is the build layer, and it overlaps this spec at SO-F-01, SO-F-08. This spec will cite those ids and keep only what the fold does not cover; trim pending fold PR (the final fold ids come in a separate pull request, branch contracts/scope-one-fold-build-layer). Nothing is trimmed yet. Owner decisions of 31 Oct 2026 apply: crdt-merge stays in its own repository and is reached only across the WO-05-A call-out boundary (never vendored, no memev-merge); tiers are free core, Personal at $12/month or $120/year for up to 3 computers, and contact us above that; there is no Federated tier.

tasks.title: Equivocation and suspicious-contribution handler: evidence goes to Memev authority and exclusion policy
requirements: MV-TRU-07: Equivocation and suspicious contributions are detected and handed to Memev authority and exclusion policy. (source: owner notes of 31 Oct 2026, docs/scope-one/programme/REQUIREMENTS.md:56; evidence docs/scope-one/programme/DECOMPOSITION.md:99; baseline 8.5)

Equivocation and admission invariants: the key is convicted, not the message; the trust anchor comes from outside the artefact; duplicates are removed on semantic identity, not signature bytes; an identity with two entries in one round is excluded entirely at admission; validity is evaluated at read time; trust signals track conduct, not distance from consensus (source: converge src/receipts.py and tests/test_receipts.py, described only, itself a port of the acfa-rs accountability core; repository analysis of 1 Nov 2026, section 3.4 item C2)
tasks.description: Repo: memev. The invariants are written as fresh tests in test/exclusion.test.mjs.
